question: A 36-year-old man was referred to the Surgery office after urgent drainage of perianal abscess two months before, persisting suppuration. The patient was being previously studied for digestive by diarrhea, abdominal pain and weight loss. Colonoscopy: Rectum of normal appearance; at the level of the descending colon and sigma, alternating areas with a "cobbled" appearance and linear and deep ulcers alternate with normal-looking ones. Endoanal echo and MRI were completed with a high transsphincter fistula. Without current medical treatment. What would be the most appropriate initial treatment of the fistula?

options.opb: Placement of non-cutting line in the course of the fistula associated with treatment with metronidazole, infliximab and immunosuppressants.
options.opc: Perform repeated drains every time an abscess occurs, associating treatment with infliximab and immunosuppressants.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: High transsphincter fistula identified on imaging -> Complex fistula requiring specialized treatment -> Consideration of treatment options based on the complexity of the fistula -> 80%
CHAIN: Alternating areas with a "cobbled" appearance and deep ulcers seen on colonoscopy -> Suggestive of Crohn's disease involvement -> Need for medical management to control inflammation -> 75%
CHAIN: Persistent suppuration after urgent drainage of perianal abscess -> Indication of ongoing infection -> Importance of addressing the underlying cause to prevent recurrence -> 85%
CHAIN: Absence of current medical treatment -> Need for initiation of appropriate therapy to manage the fistula -> Consideration of medical and surgical options -> 70%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation with a high transsphincter fistula and findings suggestive of Crohn's disease on colonoscopy indicate a complex fistula requiring specialized treatment and the need for medical management to control inflammation. Given the ongoing infection and absence of current medical treatment, the most appropriate initial treatment would involve a combination of medical therapy with metronidazole, infliximab, and immunosuppressants, along with placement of a non-cutting seton in the course of the fistula to promote healing and prevent recurrence.
analysis: The patient's presentation with a high transsphincter fistula and findings suggestive of Crohn's disease on colonoscopy indicate a complex fistula requiring specialized treatment. Given the ongoing infection and absence of current medical treatment, the most appropriate initial treatment would involve a combination of medical therapy with metronidazole, infliximab, and immunosuppressants, along with placement of a non-cutting seton in the course of the fistula to promote healing and prevent recurrence. This approach addresses both the infection and the underlying inflammatory condition.
answer: placement of non-cutting line in the course of the fistula associated with treatment with metronidazole, infliximab and immunosuppressants (opb)
